programs_aiCamp_contest_intro: Our curriculum aligns with the AI Entrepreneurship Contest, giving students the opportunity to compete at a recognized level and showcase their innovations to industry judges.
programs_aiCamp_contest_modules_0: Rules interpretation and problem statement refinement
programs_aiCamp_contest_modules_1: Business plan and technical documentation coaching
programs_aiCamp_contest_optional: We offer an optional 12-hour competition enhancement module:
programs_aiCamp_cta_subtitle: Secure your spot in the next cohort and start building the future with AI.
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_onlyCoders_ans: No. This is an entrepreneurship and product development program. Teams are cross-functional, with roles in design, business, and communication alongside technical work. Technical depth is supported but not required to participate and succeed.
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_onlyCoders_que: Is this only for advanced coders?
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_services_answe: Ithaca offers a range of programs including the EV Challenge, AI Entrepreneurship Camp, Engineering Projects, AI Pioneers Interview, Summer and Winter Camps, and Ithaca Night events.
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_takeaway_answe: Students receive a complete six-item package: an innovation project, MVP demo video and market-validation brief, pitch deck and video, growth report, social-media coverage, and alumni-community access. Outstanding students may also receive mentor recommendation letters.
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_takeaway_quest: What exactly do students take away?
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_whatIsIthaca_a: Ithaca Family Academy is a youth organization empowering young people to explore the future and build the skills to thrive in the AI era. Students learn through real-world projects: building, testing, collaborating, and presenting.
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_when_answer: The program runs from January 10 to March 28, 2026. Main classes are held from 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM, with an optional contest coaching session from 3:00 PM to 4:00 PM. Pitch Day is scheduled for April 2026 (date TBD).
programs_aiCamp_faq_items_whoCanParticip: Students in Grades 4 through 12 are eligible to join our programs. We group participants by age and experience level to ensure the best learning environment for everyone.
Who can participate in Ithaca programs?
programs_aiCamp_goals_footer: Through our dual path, students move from idea to product, from pitch to real contests, entering future careers with greater maturity.
programs_aiCamp_goals_items_competitive_: Students develop real-world entrepreneurship capabilities by working through a rigorous innovation pipeline, from problem discovery to customer validation to investor-ready pitching.
programs_aiCamp_goals_items_exposure_des: Through field trips to leading financial institutions and hands-on workshops, students gain first-hand exposure to the intersection of technology and business innovation.
programs_aiCamp_goals_items_mentors_desc: Students connect with professionals from engineering, AI, and finance. Outstanding participants may receive mentor recommendation letters for university applications.
programs_aiCamp_goals_items_mentors_titl: Access to a high-value mentor community
programs_aiCamp_goals_items_portfolio_de: Each team delivers a complete project package: an innovation prototype, MVP demo video, market-validation brief, pitch deck, growth report, and social-media coverage materials.
programs_aiCamp_hero_subtitle: From first idea to investor-ready pitch in 13 weeks. For students in Grades 8 through 12.
programs_aiCamp_meta_description: A 13-week program where students build AI-powered startups, develop MVPs, and pitch to real investors.
programs_aiCamp_meta_title: AI Entrepreneurship Camp | Ithaca Family Academy
programs_aiCamp_overview_p1: As AI transforms every industry, computational thinking and entrepreneurial skills have become critical for the next generation. The Ithaca AI Entrepreneurship Camp equips students with hands-on experience in AI application, business innovation, and project incubation.
programs_aiCamp_overview_p2: Our inaugural cohort ran from September to November 2025 in collaboration with the University of Waterloo AI Team. The second cohort begins January 10, 2026 and continues through June, withthe final roadshow scheduled for June 13, 2026. Our teams participated and won the AIEC 2026 Grand Prize.. The third cohort will be held from September to December 2026, with the final roadshow scheduled for December 2026. The teams from the third cohort will continue to prepare for and participate in AIEC 2027.
programs_aiCamp_overview_p3: Students move from idea to product, from pitch to real contests, entering future careers with greater maturity.
programs_aiCamp_structure_details_classH: 1:00 PM - 3:00 PM Main Class; 3:00 PM - 4:00 PM Contest Coaching
programs_aiCamp_structure_fieldTrips_des: During March Break, students visit leading financial institutions including {fidelity}, {vanguard}, {russell}, and the {rbc}. These visits provide first-hand exposure to the intersection of technology and finance.
programs_aiCamp_team_educators_descripti: Our teaching team blends classroom expertise with hands-on engineering practice. Instructors guide students through core concepts, workshop safety, and disciplined project execution, helping them build confidence, troubleshoot effectively, and develop strong learning habits through structured feedback and coaching.
programs_aiCamp_team_mentors_description: We invite professionals from engineering, AI, and related industries to mentor, review student work, and share real-world perspectives. Students learn what high standards look like through guest sessions, portfolio reviews, and community connections.
programs_eliteInterview_cta_subtitle: Secure your spot in the 2026 Fall cohort and start building a research portfolio that matters.
programs_eliteInterview_faq_items_contac: Our mentors provide guaranteed initial introductions to domain experts. Students also develop their own outreach skills through guided cold-contact exercises. All interviews follow consent and likeness-release protocols.
programs_eliteInterview_faq_items_experi: No. The research phase covers methodology, interview technique, and documentary production basics. Students learn by doing, with mentor guidance at every step.
Do students need prior interview or filmmaking experience?
programs_eliteInterview_faq_items_langua: All deliverables are produced in English. Interviews may be conducted in either language depending on the guest. Classroom instruction is primarily in English.
Is the program conducted in English or Chinese?
programs_eliteInterview_faq_items_takeaw: Two portfolio-ready deliverables in English: a research report suitable for university applications, and an 8-12 minute documentary that is publicly released. Both demonstrate real-world research and communication skills.
programs_eliteInterview_faq_items_whatIs: A research and documentary program where students investigate a major societal question through real interviews with experts in academia, industry, and policy. Each student claims one research track and contributes to a team documentary.
What is the Ithaca Dialogues program?
programs_eliteInterview_hero_description: Connecting students with people shaping the future. Ten weeks of fieldwork. Five research angles. One documentary.
programs_eliteInterview_meta_description: A 10-week research and documentary program where students investigate AI and Canada's future through interviews with experts in academia, industry, and policy.
programs_eliteInterview_produce_disclaim: All interviews follow formal consent and likeness-release protocols. Guests confirm before publication. Screening events are open to families.
programs_eliteInterview_produce_document: Interview footage, narration, and data visualization. Edited and publicly released.
programs_eliteInterview_produce_report_d: Literature review, interview evidence, and original conclusions. Directly usable as a university application portfolio piece.
programs_eliteInterview_question_body: Geoffrey Hinton in Toronto. Yoshua Bengio in Montreal. Deep learning was born here. Yet commercialization, talent, and productivity have steadily migrated south. This is the question your team will investigate, and the story your documentary will tell.
programs_eliteInterview_question_quote: “Canada pioneered deep learning. Why hasn’t that translated into economic leadership?”
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_items_cap: World-class research, scale-up fatigue. From Element AI to Cohere.
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_items_edu: Is Ontario preparing high schoolers for the AI era? You are the stakeholder on this one.
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_items_ind: Banks, hospitals, farms still struggle to adopt AI. What is blocking real productivity gains?
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_items_pol: From $20B in sovereign compute to “AI for All” - do government milestones actually work?
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_items_tal: Why does top AI talent keep flowing south? Is immigration policy a trump card or an illusion?
programs_eliteInterview_tracks_subtitle: Each student claims one track and owns it for the semester.
programs_eliteInterview_whyNow_descripti: On June 4, 2026, the federal government released its national AI strategy “AI for All.” An entire semester of student research coincides with the nation asking the same questions.
programs_evChallenge_competition_descrip: Organized by the University of Waterloo Faculty of Engineering, the EV Challenge is a high school electric vehicle endurance race. Teams design, build, and drive their own EVs, evaluated on engineering quality, vehicle performance, driving strategy, and team collaboration.
programs_evChallenge_cta_subtitle: Join the Ithaca EV Team and be part of a team that designs, builds, and races an electric vehicle.
programs_evChallenge_faq_items_experienc: No. The program teaches everything from the ground up. Roles span engineering design, assembly, test driving, and team operations. Every team member contributes regardless of technical background.
programs_evChallenge_faq_items_schedule_: Sessions run bi-weekly on Saturdays from September 2026 through May 2027. Morning session covers 10:00 AM to 12:00 PM, afternoon session runs 1:00 PM to 3:00 PM.
What does the schedule look like?
programs_evChallenge_faq_items_takeaway_: Beyond the EV itself, students gain project management skills, technical documentation experience, presentation abilities, and real sponsorship negotiation practice. These are portfolio-ready experiences for university applications.
What will my child take away?
programs_evChallenge_faq_items_whatIsWat: An electric vehicle endurance race organized by the University of Waterloo Faculty of Engineering. High school teams design, build, and race their own EVs. The 2027 competition is scheduled for late May.
What is the Waterloo EV Challenge?
programs_evChallenge_faq_items_whoCanJoi: Students in Grades 8 through 11 in the Greater Toronto Area. We welcome anyone interested in engineering, automotive technology, or team-based projects. No prior experience is required.
Who can join the EV team?
programs_evChallenge_gains_items_busines: Fundraising, sponsorship acquisition, resource management, and the experience of building a team from scratch.
programs_evChallenge_gains_items_enginee: Design thinking, hands-on fabrication, and cross-discipline collaboration on a vehicle that actually races.
programs_evChallenge_gains_items_univers: A distinctive portfolio piece for top engineering and business programs across North America.
programs_evChallenge_hero_subtitle: Design and build a real electric vehicle. Run a team. Compete at the Waterloo EV Challenge.
programs_evChallenge_mission_description: We build an EV, run a team, and race at competition. Through engineering and business training, we prepare the next generation of builders, operators, and leaders.
programs_evChallenge_mission_quote: "When you set out for Ithaca, hope the voyage is long, full of adventure, full of discovery."
programs_evChallenge_mission_title: We don't just build a car.
programs_evChallenge_model3d_business_de: Run the team as a real operation. Sponsorship acquisition, budget management, logistics coordination, and organizational skills that make a racing team function.
programs_evChallenge_model3d_canvasAriaL: Interactive 3D wireframe of the Ithaca EV trike and program tracks
programs_evChallenge_model3d_engineering: Design, build, and test a functioning electric vehicle. CAD modeling, chassis fabrication, electrical wiring, battery systems, and iterative performance testing.
programs_evChallenge_model3d_machineDesc: Custom-built electric trike. Aluminum tube frame. Designed and assembled by students.
programs_evChallenge_model3d_sectionAria: The Ithaca EV trike and program tracks
programs_evChallenge_pastSeasons_subtitl: From first welds to race day at Waterloo.
programs_evChallenge_workshopToRoles_rol: Hands-on fabrication, component integration, and systematic performance validation on the vehicle.
CAD modeling, structural analysis, and electrical systems layout for the EV chassis and powertrain.
Sponsorship outreach, budget planning, logistics coordination, and cross-functional project management.
Track testing protocols, endurance race strategy, and driver skill development under competition conditions.
